chunk_map.heading: Every task maps onto the same six phases

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a referent nobody can resolve breaks comprehension mid-deck. Chunk 1's 'them'/'across them' (line 5) resolves to 'six phases' one clause earlier in the same sentence; the six bold-led bullets (lines 9-14) each define their own term inline. Chunk 2's 'this territory' (line 99) resolves against chunk 0's title 'The whole map' plus chunk 1's 'cycle'/'six phases'; 'the near half'/'the far half' (lines 100-101) are defined the sentence they're introduced in and reused ('here'/'there') within the same chunk. No forward references, no orphaned pronouns. Harm absent.
No pointer to another file, by position or otherwise, occurs anywhere in the body (lines 1-101).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a dead beat reference strands a student who goes looking for something that isn't there. Line 99 'M1 was the first step into this territory' names the real, current preceding module in general terms, not a specific missing exercise/lecture beat that could go stale on a re-chunk. No 'the X you did/saw' construction is present. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal demo instruction occurs anywhere in this container lecture.

Chunk 1 (lines 3-95) carries the full figure, six defined phases, and the places-not-pipeline closer; chunk 2 (lines 97-101) carries three self-carrying orientation bullets (M1 recap, near-half definition, far-half definition). Neither is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

'Every task maps onto the same six phases' (line 3) is confirmed by the body's own 'Every piece of agentic work maps onto the same cycle. Six phases' (line 5) and the six-bullet enumeration that follows. 'You are here' (line 97) is confirmed by the chunk's orientation content (M1 recap, near/far half split) — the chunk does place the reader.

No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere in body. No anaphora/epistrophe triple. No self-grading superlative (no 'one of the most useful' phrasing). No number-with-own-retraction. No abstraction-noun stack. The SVG label text's short verb chains ('act · read the result · correct' line 70; 'run · let it fail · shape the verifier · re-run' line 69; 'read · judge · gate what ships · by hand for now' line 71) are each concrete on every leg, not empty-leg triplets.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: maintainer/repo vocabulary lands where a room full of engineers cannot parse it. No repo-internal dialect term (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood-as-noun, Connections) appears anywhere in body or SVG label text (lines 1-101, 7-86). The nine loop names in the SVG (THE CONTEXT LOOP, THE PLAN LOOP, etc.) are this training's own coined pedagogical vocabulary, not maintainer-internal editorial dialect. Harm absent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 1's six phase-definition bullets (lines 9-14) each carry exactly one short bolded handle (**Intent.** through **Outcome.**, each ≤5 words), matching the rule's own 'a law/consolidation slide may carry one handle per law' allowance, and the file's own maintainer block (line 120) names this exact carve-out. Chunk 2 carries no bold at all, matching the maintainer block's explicit note that 'You are here' carries none.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a lecture, so headings must be claims, not imperative/label. 'Every task maps onto the same six phases' (line 3) is a declarative claim the body then substantiates. 'You are here' (line 97) is grammatically a declarative sentence (subject + verb + locative complement), not a bare noun-phrase label ('Overview', 'Background') — it reads closer to the rule's own claim examples than to a label, though it is a conventional map-orientation phrase rather than a substantive assertion. Flagging per dispatch instruction as a note for the pending corpus-wide rule-15 decision rather than an individual REVISE, since the same phrase shape recurs at this exact structural beat across the corpus (map-opener 'you are here' orientation slides) and a per-file call here would pre-empt that decision.
